brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut to ₹0.65–0.80/pc on caps, backed by market-fair pricing and four credible backup suppliers ready to quote.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹0.65–0.80/pc on 28 mm induction-wad PP caps at higher volumes
priceAsk.basis: Market research shows typical pricing is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser specs; verdict: MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom. We spend ₹44.37 L annually and can shift volume to any of four qualified alternates who do rigid pharma packaging.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep current 30 Days After Receipt; no change needed

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana publishes no financials, so we can't see inside their books. That means our leverage comes from our own wallet and our backup plan. We spend ₹44.37 L a year with them — meaningful volume for a private packager. We have four strong alternates lined up: Mold-Tek (listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader), Hitech Corporation (listed, broad bottle/cap capability), Pearl Polymers (listed PET specialist), and Manjushree Technopack (India's largest rigid converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100). With those options live, we can push firmly on price without worrying about supply gaps.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader doing pails, containers, pharma — strong and profitable; robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging firm; broad capability across bottles and caps

risks: Rachana's financials aren't public, so we can't gauge their cash position or staying power — run a credit check or site audit before locking in sole-source volume.

We have no internal price benchmark (no bestPriceWePay figure) for rigid packaging from other vendors — the market ask is our only anchor, so verify it with two more quotes before finalising the target.
Pushing too hard without a formal RFQ to the alternates means Rachana might call our bluff — issue parallel RFQs to Manjushree and Mold-Tek this month to make the threat real.
If Rachana resists on price, watch for them to tighten lead times or MOQs as a backdoor way to claw back margin — nail down service levels in writing.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've reviewed our packaging spend and the market — we'd like to work toward ₹0.65–0.80 per cap at our volumes, and we're talking to three other rigid-packaging suppliers this quarter to benchmark.
